The 10-Q balance sheet (pf_10q_20260911, reading/10q_2026-09-11.txt line ~291-333) shows current $7,625M and non-current $117,712M; the 10-Q fair-value note gives $125.0B of senior notes and borrowings at 2026-08-31. findings.finding: Guidance-track basis mismatch: two rows for Q4 FY2026 non-GAAP EPS with different actuals (2.11 and 2.03). The March-2026 guide ($1.96-$2.00 USD, mid 1.98; release_2026-03-10) excludes one-time gains; the June release reports $2.11 including one-time investment gains and $2.03 excluding them (footnote 1). The 2.11 row compares guidance to an actual on a different basis and inflates the beat.
findings.where: evidence_pack.json guidance_track: period 'Q4 FY2026', metric eps_non_gaap, actual 2.11 (source_ids pf_rel_20260310_1, pf_rel_20260610_1); the fragment that wrote it (gather/reports.json or gather/numbers.json)
findings.fix: Delete the 2.11 row; keep actual 2.03 (ex-gains, same basis as the guide).

findings.finding: Duplicate guidance_track rows after merge: Q4 FY2026 revenue, Q1 FY2027 revenue, Q1 FY2027 non-GAAP EPS and FY2026 revenue each appear twice (once from gather_numbers, once from gather_reports), so ticker-check counts n=6 revenue rows for 3 periods; FY2026 revenue's second row cites the 10-K as the reporting source, the first the June release. The numbers lane flagged this itself.
findings.where: evidence_pack.json guidance_track (duplicates from gather/reports.json vs gather/numbers.json)
findings.fix: Keep one row per (period, metric) in gather/numbers.json (owner of guidance_track per the stage file) and remove the copies from gather/reports.json; re-run ticker-prep/ticker-value.

findings.finding: FY2027 revenue guidance is 'at least $90 billion' (release_2026-09-10 line 62; June release 'confirm our prior revenue guidance of $90 billion'), a floor, but it is stored as low=high=90B and used as the current_year_revenue midpoint and as the denominator of growth_anchor (FY2028 $130B / $90B - 1 = 44.4%). Treating a floor as a point is acceptable only if labelled; mixing the 2025-10-16 FAM FY2028 target (built on FY27E $85B, constant currency) with the raised FY27 floor makes the 44.4% FY28 growth a hybrid of two vintages and two bases.
findings.fix: Mark rp_g_fy27_rev as a floor (note 'at least'); state in growth_anchor.reason that FY28 $130B is the Oct-2025 constant-currency target on an $85B FY27 base, and either anchor the FY28 growth on the FAM path ($85B->$130B = 52.9%) or on the $130B level, not a ratio of mixed vintages. Recheck after the 2026-10-28 Investor Day 8-K becomes citable (2026-10-30).

findings.finding: Long-term guidance (FY2028-FY2030 revenue $130B/$185B/$225B, non-GAAP EPS $10.65/$16.00/$21.00, OCI $73B/$114B/$144B) all comes from the Financial Analyst Meeting deck of 2025-10-16 (rp_fam2025), more than a year old; an 8-K with Investor Day material was filed 2026-10-28 (Items 7.01/9.01) and is not citable until 2026-10-30, so the targets may already be superseded. Values traced correctly to the deck (gather/raw_reports/fam2025_kehring.txt), but they are stated in constant currency and non-GAAP; growth_half_life rests on this one source.
findings.where: evidence_pack.json guidance rp_g_fy28_rev_fam, rp_g_fy29_rev_fam, rp_g_fy30_rev_fam, rp_g_fy28..fy30_eps_fam, rp_g_fy27..fy30_oci; drivers.growth_anchor, drivers.growth_half_life
findings.fix: Show next to the result that the long-term path is the Oct-2025 target and that the 2026-10-28 update is not yet citable; rerun with as_of >= 2026-10-30 and replace the rows with the updated targets if changed.
